note: SYNTHETIC DATA: real university names are attached to invented policies and statements. This file describes the project's tests, not findings.

requirements.text: `.claude/settings.json` registers command hooks for UserPromptSubmit, Stop, PreCompact, SessionStart, and SessionEnd, all calling `.claude/hooks/log_event.py` via `$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR`.

`log_event.py` reads hook JSON from stdin and appends one line to `logs/events.jsonl`: `{ts (ISO, local tz), event, session_id, phase (contents of .phase or "untagged"), payload}`.
- UserPromptSubmit: payload.prompt = full prompt text
- Stop: payload.response_excerpt = the last assistant text in transcript_path (first 1,000 chars)
- PreCompact: payload.trigger (manual/auto)
- SessionStart: payload.source (startup/resume/clear/compact/fork)
- SessionEnd: payload.reason
The hook never blocks Claude Code. It always exits 0, writes nothing to stdout on UserPromptSubmit (stdout there is injected into context), and logs its own errors to `logs/hook_errors.log`.

On SessionEnd and PreCompact, copy the session transcript to `raw_logs/transcripts/` (gitignored) so token data survives local cleanup of transcripts. Also copy that session's subagent transcripts (`<session>/subagents/*.jsonl` and `*.meta.json` next to the transcript) to `raw_logs/transcripts/subagents/<session_id>/`. `log_event.py --backfill-subagents` copies any still on disk.
Before writing the hook, check the current Claude Code hooks docs for exact field names and record what you confirmed in docs/progress.md.
Makefile targets (stubs are fine for now): `data analysis test report tokens timeline site serve clean`.
`make test` runs pytest and writes a machine-readable run file to `results/tests/` (format in P4).
Tests for log_event.py feed it sample JSON for each event type and check the output lines.

Before anything is written to `logs/`, `log_event.py` redacts every string in the record: emails become `[EMAIL]`; API keys/tokens (`sk-…`, `ghp_…`, `github_pat_…`, `Bearer <token>`) become `[REDACTED_TOKEN]`; absolute home paths (`‹redacted-path›`, `/home/<name>`) become `~`. This also applies to `hook_errors.log`. It has its own tests.
`src/data/generate.py --seed 2026` is deterministic: the same seed produces byte-identical files.

`data/raw/institutions.csv` has 150 rows. Names are real US university names taken from `data/reference/real_universities.txt` (~150 real US universities with CS programs, `Name | ST` per line), one per institution with no duplicates, matched to the institution's state where possible. The policies, courses and statements attached to them are invented (HUMAN spec change, 2026-11-10). Columns: inst_id, name, state, census_region, control (public/private), carnegie (R1/R2/Masters/Baccalaureate), cs_enrollment.

`data/raw/statements.csv` has ~350 official-publication excerpts (0–4 per institution). Columns: stmt_id, inst_id, pub_type (policy_page/news/strategic_plan/syllabus_template/faq), pub_date (2023-01 to 2026-10), text (2–5 sentences assembled from phrase banks, keyed to hidden labels).

`data/raw/courses.csv` has ~2,000 course-term rows. Columns: course_id, inst_id, code, title, level (intro/intermediate/upper/graduate), is_se (bool), term (F23…F26), policy (0 prohibited, 1 limited use, 2 permitted with disclosure, 3 encouraged, 4 integrated/required), disclosure_required, assessment_adaptation (none/in_class_exams/oral_defense/process_logs/ai_critique), tools_named (drawn from a fixed list of generic tool categories: chat assistant, IDE autocomplete, agentic coding tool), allowed_uses (multi-label, semicolon-separated: explanation;debugging;code_generation;testing;writing; empty when policy = 0).
Hidden labels and planted effects go only in `data/raw/ground_truth.json`. Analysis code must never read this file (enforced by a test that greps src/analysis/).
Intro courses are more restrictive than upper-level courses.
SE courses are more permissive than non-SE courses at the same level.
Permissiveness rises with each term.
R1 departments have a more positive statement stance.
Planted null: control (public/private) has no effect on policy. This checks for false positives.
Learning vs producing: intro courses that allow AI mostly allow explanation and debugging, rarely code_generation. SE courses are the most likely to allow code_generation and testing.
Assessment shift: the more restrictive a course's policy, the more likely it uses in-class exams or oral defenses. Process logs and AI-critique assignments mostly show up in courses with policy ≥ 2.
Rhetoric gap: about 15% of institutions get a deliberate mismatch, with an enthusiastic official stance but restrictive courses, or the reverse. Flag them in ground_truth.json only.
Statement labels (stance −2..+2, mentions_collaboration, mentions_integrity, mentions_careers) are correlated with the planted effects in documented ways.
8% of policies missing at random, inconsistent casing in `level`, ~1% duplicate rows, some statements that mention both integrity concerns and collaboration.
Schema tests: types, allowed values, row counts within ±10%, referential integrity.
`docs/data-dictionary.md` documents every column and states that the data is synthetic.
Cleaning (`src/analysis/clean.py`): dedupe, normalize casing, keep missing policy as NA (no imputation), write `data/clean/`. Log row counts before and after.

Codebook `docs/codebook.md` defines stance and theme codes with inclusion/exclusion rules and examples. `code_text.py` applies it with transparent rules (keyword/phrase patterns, no LLM calls), so every coding decision can be traced to a rule.

Coder vs ground truth: per-label precision/recall/F1 and a stance confusion matrix. Target macro-F1 ≥ 0.80. If it falls short, report the actual number honestly. Do not tune against the test set: split statements into a dev half (for tuning rules) and a held-out half (for reporting), using the dev/held-out split defined in `docs/data-dictionary.md`. Coder rules may only be tuned on the dev half; a test fails if the coder code reads held-out labels. Only `src/evaluation/` (and tests) may read ground truth.

Human agreement (HUMAN task): generate `data/reference/hand_code_sample.csv` with 30 held-out statements and blank label columns. The sample is coded by Aayush. Report Cohen's kappa as "Aayush vs coder" and "Aayush vs truth".

Descriptives with 95% bootstrap CIs (2,000 resamples, fixed seed): policy distribution by level, by is_se, by term, by census_region, and overall; stance and theme prevalence by carnegie, year, census_region, and overall. (census_region and overall added in P3 at Aayush's direction, for the dashboard.)
Association: chi-square + Cramér's V for policy × level and policy × is_se.
Ordinal logistic regression: policy ~ level + is_se + term_index + control + carnegie (statsmodels OrderedModel). Report coefficients, 95% CIs, and n used.
Recovery tests: estimated directions match DATA-06..09, and the DATA-10 null is not significant at α = 0.05. These tests may read ground_truth.json; analysis code may not.
`results/` JSON files follow schemas in `src/report/schemas/`, validated by tests.

Allowed-uses analysis (RQ6): prevalence of each use by level and by is_se, with bootstrap CIs. A recovery test checks that the intro-course gap between explanation/debugging and code_generation (DATA-15) shows up.
Assessment analysis (RQ7): assessment_adaptation by policy level and course level, with chi-square and Cramér's V.

Rhetoric vs practice (RQ8): per institution, compare coded statement stance with mean course permissiveness (both standardized). Report the correlation and list institutions whose gap is in the top decile. A recovery test checks how many of the DATA-17 mismatched institutions land in that list (report precision/recall).

Clustering: course-term rows are nested in courses and institutions, so they are not independent. Every inferential result on course data (ANL-05 CIs, ANL-07 regression, ANL-08 recovery and null tests, ANL-11, ANL-12) must account for clustering by `inst_id`. Use cluster-robust (sandwich) SEs, a mixed model with an institution random effect, or a cluster bootstrap that resamples institutions. `docs/methods.md` states which method was used for each result. A test checks that the DATA-10 null stays non-significant under the clustered method, since naive row-level tests can flag sampling noise in institution effects as a real effect.
`docs/methods.md` describes the approach in plain language, including the limits of synthetic data and keyword coding.
Static page that loads `site/data/*.json` (copied from results/ by `make site`). Chart.js pinned to an exact version via CDN. No build step.

A visible synthetic-data banner on every view: "Synthetic data: real university names are attached to invented policies and statements. Nothing here describes what these schools actually do." (wording changed by HUMAN, 2026-11-10).

Views: KPI summary; policy distribution by level (stacked bars); SE vs non-SE; trend by term; census-region comparison (no state map: with ~3 synthetic institutions per state, state averages are just noise); allowed-uses heatmap (use × course level, RQ6); assessment-changes chart by policy level (RQ7); rhetoric-vs-practice scatter, one dot per institution with stance on one axis and course permissiveness on the other (RQ8); stance and theme prevalence; regression coefficient plot with CIs; coder accuracy panel (ANL-03/04).
Statement explorer: full-text search plus filters by stance, theme, pub_type, and year. Shows coded labels next to the text so readers can judge the coder.
Each chart has a one-sentence takeaway, a "data table" toggle, and a link to its JSON source.
Color-blind-safe palette, keyboard navigable, works at 375px width, light and dark mode.

Institution drilldown: pick one institution and see its course policies next to its official statements, so you can spot departments whose rhetoric doesn't match their actual course rules. Clicking a dot in the rhetoric-vs-practice scatter opens that institution here.
Tests: every number displayed matches results JSON; a headless browser (Playwright for Python) loads each view with no console errors and finds each chart canvas populated.

A conftest plugin writes `results/tests/run-<timestamp>.json` per run. For each test it records: nodeid, req_ids, phase, kind (unit/property/integration/recovery/ui/fault), status, duration_s, failure message, and `body_sha256`. The test's docstring and source code are stored once per content hash in the sidecar `results/tests/bodies/<body_sha256>.json`, which is written only if absent, so an unchanged test adds no new text. Run files from before this change (schema test-run/1) hold docstring and source inline; readers accept both formats.
Keep every run file and every body file. The explorer shows the latest run plus pass/fail history per test.
Traceability matrix: parse requirement lines from specs/*.md. Show requirement → tests → status. Requirements with no tests are shown in red. Coverage % from pytest-cov is shown per module.

Fault injection (`make faults`): on a temp copy of the repo, apply ≥8 deliberate bugs (e.g. flip a regression sign, skip dedupe, change seed handling, break a keyword rule, off-by-one in term index), run the suite, and record which tests caught each one. Report a fault detection rate. Uncaught faults are listed, not hidden.
Explorer UI: search; filter by phase, kind, status, and requirement; click a test to see its docstring, source, history, and linked spec text.
Claims page: each finding on the dashboard links to the tests that support it.
Renders `docs/review-log.md` (Aayush's manual reviews) next to the automated evidence.
The explorer's own data loading and filters have tests (Playwright).

`make timeline` merges logs/events.jsonl, docs/progress.md, git log, and docs/review-log.md into `site/timeline/data/timeline.json`. Every item has ts, actor (HUMAN | CLAUDE | shared), phase, type, summary, and source.

Actor attribution rules: prompts, `human:` commits, review-log entries, and spec edits are HUMAN. Responses, `agent:` commits, and generated code are CLAUDE. Ambiguous items are labelled "shared"; never guess. Logged prompts are further classified: human-typed (the prompt starts with "Typed by me"); automated (subagent reports, scheduled tasks, cross-session messages); shared if unclear.
Timeline view: zoomable vertical timeline with filters for actor, phase, and type, and clear/compact markers.
Q&A view: each prompt paired with the response excerpt that followed it, searchable.

Contribution summary: counts per actor (prompts, approvals, rejected plans, spec edits, reviews, commits, lines changed), plus a short narrative that Aayush writes (docs/timeline-narrative.md). Approvals are the HUMAN decision tags in docs/progress.md. Rejected plans are the REJECTED: tags in docs/progress.md; history before that tag existed is shown as "not recorded".
Redaction pass before anything reaches site/: strip absolute home paths, emails, tokens, and keys. A test scans site/ for these patterns.

Before writing the parser, inspect one real transcript in raw_logs/transcripts/ and record the actual usage field names in docs/progress.md (expected: input, output, cache-creation, and cache-read tokens per assistant message).
`make tokens` produces one row per assistant message: ts, session_id, model, the four token counts, and phase/activity (joined from the nearest preceding UserPromptSubmit event in logs/events.jsonl).
Session boundaries: mark /clear (SessionStart source=clear) and /compact (PreCompact) events.

Metrics: totals by phase and by activity (planning, data, analysis, writing-code, validation, docs); tokens per prompt; context size per turn (input + cache tokens), which should show a sawtooth at clears/compacts; cache-read share.

Experiment (Aayush picks a comparable small task, e.g. "add one chart"): run it in condition A, a long session with no clear; condition B, right after /clear + /resume; and condition C, right after /compact. Run each condition once (1 run per condition, per Aayush). Report the comparison and state plainly that the sample is small: with n = 1 per condition the differences are anecdotal, not evidence.
Usage-limit events on the Pro plan get logged by hand in docs/usage-limits.md and shown on the page.
Page: charts for the above, plus a "what I learned" section that Aayush writes.
Tests: parser on a fixture transcript; totals equal the sum of rows; the phase join has no gaps.
`site/index.html` landing page linking Dashboard, Validation, Timeline, Tokens, Evaluation & Reflection, and the GitHub repo.
GitHub Actions workflow deploys site/ to GitHub Pages on push to main.
Pre-publish gate (`make prepublish`): all tests pass, redaction scan clean, link check passes, synthetic banner present on every data page.
README.md explains the project, how to reproduce everything (`make all`), and the live URL.
docs/evaluation.md and the reflection are rendered as a page, unedited by Claude.
